title: General Committee Of Public Instruction
definition: The General Committee of Public Instruction was a body established by the British East India Company in 1823, primarily responsible for overseeing education in British India and administering the annual grant of one lakh rupees sanctioned under the Charter Act of 1813.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for understanding the genesis of modern Western education in India, the famous 'Orientalist-Anglicist Controversy', and the ideological battles that preceded Macaulay's Minute of 1835.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of General Committee Of Public Instruction.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Early British educational policies in India
